title: R’ Shimon ben Chananyah, a Tanna
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Tosefta Kelim Kamma 4:9, R’ Chalafta of Kefar Chananyah said, “I asked Shimon ben Chananyah, who had asked the son of R’ Chanina ben Teradion,” etc.

Yalkut, Chukat, on “Elazar shall take,” cites an occasion when R’ Yose the Galilean was sitting and expounding the red-heifer laws in Tiberias. R’ Shimon ben Chanina sat with him and discussed those laws with him at length.
In Sanhedrin 101a, R’ Shimon ben Elazar says in his name, “Whoever recites a verse at its proper time brings good to the world.” Hyman says the Rif there instead reads R’ Yehoshua B-Ch [ב״ח].

notes.text: Chananyah and Chanina are Hyman’s reported forms. The Rif’s ב״ח after Yehoshua remains an unresolved patronymic; a plausible expansion to ben Chananyah is not adopted without the passage.

The whole saved Vilna Rif Sanhedrin20a scalar0 actually has רשב״ג reporting Yehudah ben Chananyah, beside Hyman’s Shimon ben Elazar reporting Yehoshua B-Ch. It does not prove that Hyman’s ב״ח has the same expansion or that his edition had these names. No full Rabbi/Rabban is inferred from the Rif’s abbreviations. The Chalafta>Shimon>son-of-Chanina-ben-Teradion question chain remains complete, with Shimon untitled inside the quotation. Yalkut פ״א means ONCE/an occasion, not section1; no Kelim subdivision is invented. Chananyah/Chanina variants remain.

The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta Kelim Kamma 4:9 retains Chalafta’s question to Shimon and Shimon’s question to the son of Chanina ben Teradion. Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 761 names Shimon ben Chanina in the exchange with Yose the Galilean at Tiberias. The checked Bavli names Shimon ben Elazar reporting Shimon ben Chananyah. The consulted Vilna Rif gives רשב״ג reporting Yehudah ben Chananyah, while Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1176) reports Yehoshua ב״ח. The patronymic in Hyman’s Rif reading remains unexpanded, and the differently written names are retained at each occurrence.
